interpretation: Plain Tor was classified with F1 0.973 (95% CI 0.786–1.000); persona cover with F1 0.487 (95% CI 0.154–0.833). Persona cover reduced the observer's ACTIVE/IDLE F1 by 0.486 in this dataset, i.e. it made the inference task harder. Cost: the median page load was 1.04x plain Tor and the cover overhead was 5.991x the page bytes. Because the tunnel is persistent (D21) that overhead is a *rate*, not a constant: it is paid every second, so it grows the longer the user stays idle. The wire rate was 164.9 kbit/s and the observed traffic inside IDLE windows was 21336.6 B/s (plain Tor: 994.9 B/s). Constant-rate cover (B) scored F1 0.495 at 6.059x overhead; it is the baseline that persona cover has to beat on cost without giving up inference resistance.
